# dsh-agent-activity
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that makes the agent's working process visible **while it is still working
** — before the final answer lands.
The card docks right above the composer, in the same place as the todo panel, and answers three ques
ht above the composer, in the same place as the todo panel, and answers three questions at a glance:
- **What has it already done?** Every tool call of the current turn, in order, with its target and h

ow long it took (✓ / ✗ / spinner).
- **What is it doing now?** A phase label — *thinking*, *running

a tool*, *writing the answer* — plus the current step number.
- **What is it about to do?** The tool
calls the model has just announced but not yet run, followed by the next unfinished todo.
While the model streams a reply, the card also shows the leading edge of that reply, so you can tell
the difference between "thinking", "stuck" and "writing".
### Every row says *why*, then what was done
A row used to read `write file · client.js`, which tells you nothing unless you already know the cod

e — and
even `delete dist/*.tgz` only says *where*, not *why*. Each row now leads with the purpose,
delete dist/*.tgz` only says *where*, not *why*. Each row now leads with the purpose, in this order:
1. **the todo it serves** — when the agent keeps a todo list (the panel above the composer) the row

itself gave** — the sentence it was writing when it decided to call the tool;
3. **a plain-language

reason for that kind of action** — *"make sure the change did not break anything"* for
a test run, *
"clear the old package so the next release is not stale"* for deleting `dist/*.tgz`.

The concrete detail follows as small print: `run tests activity.test.mjs`, `delete dist/*.tgz`,
`sea
rch “commandPlan”`, `commit feat: x`. So the big line answers **what this step was for**, the small

line
answers **what it touched** — never the raw tool name.
When the same action on the same object repeats (three `git status` in a row), the rows collapse int

o one with
a `×N` badge instead of padding the list.
### Read the list, not the mechanics
The card now leads with the same thing the built-in **Tasks** panel above the composer leads with: t

he
list. Opened, it shows one row per todo — `✓ done`, spinner `in progress`, hollow `not started` —

and the
tool calls move down into a secondary *What I ran* section. Collapsed, the single line is t

he todo being
worked on, followed by `2 done · 1 now · 1 to go`.
Rows still carry the plain-language label (`edit “收起时是一行”`, `run tests · activity.test.mjs`), so the
two halves answer different questions: the list says **what is left**, the rows say **what that mea
halves answer different questions: the list says **what is left**, the rows say **what that meant**.
[该节后续省略]
## Why a plugin and not a skill
A skill can only add instructions to the model's context; it cannot render anything. This is a UI pl
ugin: a Host half that folds the session event log into a small "activity" projection, and a Client
half that renders it in the Harness Web UI.
## What it renders

The card speaks in plain language instead of tool names: what happened, what is happening
now, and w

hat is queued. It deliberately does **not** echo your message — the transcript right
above already s
hows it. The collapsed line is one stable row:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Click it and the panel opens as a floating overlay above the card (Escape, outside click or
a second
click closes it) — opening it never changes the page layout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Every row carries the reason the agent gave for that step — the sentence it wrote right before the
c

all, quoted back as 为了 …. When the agent said nothing (or the step is a long scripted chain),
the ca

rd falls back to the todo item it is currently working on, so a row is never just
"跑脚本 · x.py" with

ck to the todo item it is currently working on, so a row is never just
"跑脚本 · x.py" with no purpose.

That is the whole point: **plain words**, then a recap of what the agent did for the task
(`改文件 3 ·

跑测试 2 · 发版 1`), then the rows and what is queued. No API names — `npm test`
reads 跑测试, `"$NODE" --ch

eck lib/client.js` reads 检查语法 · client.js, `curl -o x.tgz …`
reads 下载文件 · x.tgz, `git push` reads 提交

代码. A file path collapses to its last two
segments, a search shows its quoted term, and a command th

at cannot be classified shows
执行命令 next to the command itself — never a vague label with no informat

ion. Tool names
survive only in the hover tooltip. Wording follows the UI language (Chinese and Engl

ish),
long rows wrap to two lines, and the answer preview keeps its line breaks.

If the agent also keeps a todo list, the panel shows it as a checklist under
「为了完成你的要求，我打算」 with ✓ d

one / ⠋ running / ○ pending — that is the plan in the
agent's own words, so it leads the panel whene

g / ○ pending — that is the plan in the
agent's own words, so it leads the panel whenever it exists.
## How it works
- **Host** (`lib/index.js`, `lib/activity.js`) registers the session projection `activity` with a si
ngle `apply(state, event)` fold over the durable event log: `turn/start`, `step/start`, `assistant/m
essage`, `tool/call`, `tool/result`, `turn/end`. The fold is pure and synchronous, returns the same
state reference for events it does not care about, and keeps a bounded log (32 tool calls) so long t

urns stay cheap.
- **Wire** (`wire.view`) hands the finished value to the Client. The Client never f
olds events itself — it reads `useProjection("activity")` and, for the plan row, the built-in `todos

` projection.
- Because the projection is registered at boot and has no persisted rows yet, sessions
restored from an older checkpoint simply re-fold their log through `init` + `apply`; no migration i
from an older checkpoint simply re-fold their log through `init` + `apply`; no migration is needed.
